items.excerpt: A practical setup guide for wiring Figma, Jira, GitLab and Playwright MCP servers into a coding agent, covering the different auth models and what each server actually exposes. Positions the Figma MCP server as the design-context bridge in an agent toolchain.

In Figma Make a designer can describe a checkout flow in plain English and watch working code appear — which moves shipping power to design but leaves ownership of failures unresolved. Argues teams need explicit accountability rules once design output becomes production code.

Most AI integrations fail because they interrupt an existing workflow instead of improving it. Lays out which AI affordances users actually adopt and how to place them so the feature earns its interface real estate.

Cline is now available in the AI SDK harness layer through the @ai-sdk/harness-cline adapter, built with the Cline team. Any harness-compatible agent can now be run through the same HarnessAgent interface, making agent backends swappable in product and prototype builds.

Pro and Enterprise teams can connect Cursor Origin repositories to Vercel so agent-authored pull requests automatically get Preview Deployments and production deploys on merge. Closes the loop between an IDE agent and a reviewable, shareable UI build.

Canva now ships AI code and app building to every user, yet professional designers still treat it as an embarrassing tool. Asks whether the industry's status hierarchy of design software survives when the 'amateur' tool has the same generative capabilities.

A refresher on human-computer interaction principles and interaction types, framed for designers working on conversational, voice and agentic interfaces. Useful grounding as HCI fundamentals get re-applied to AI-native product surfaces.

Lea Verou pushes back on three-state light/dark/system toggles, arguing two states plus a correct default covers every real color-scheme scenario. A concrete token-and-theming decision that design systems keep getting wrong.

Leo AI CEO Maor Farid argues mechanical engineering has crossed a 'mechanical Turing test' threshold — AI-generated designs are now indistinguishable from human-made manufacturable parts, citing a 791% rise in positive user responses by July.

Incremental agent pilots are fine, but the payoff only lands when teams use them as a bridge to redesigning the process itself. A caution against bolting agents onto existing design and documentation workflows unchanged.

The more valuable and complex a design process becomes, the more important it is to define exactly where the machine stops and the person takes over. Frames human-in-the-loop handoff points as the highest-leverage AI design decision.

HeyGears' G1X brings full-colour resin 3D printing to the desktop at a sub-£3,000 Kickstarter price. Lowers the cost of turning generated or CAD-authored concepts into colour-accurate physical prototypes.

ArtDeck is a new $6 visual reference board app for art, animation and motion graphics that adds video support, colour sampling, measurement and onion-skinning. A PureRef alternative aimed at reference-heavy concept and lookdev workflows.

A procedural coral growth simulation showing generative/algorithmic growth rules producing organic geometry. A reminder that rule-driven generation, not just prompt-driven models, still produces the most controllable procedural form.

Adobe walks through turning a single source image into a full set of on-brand assets using Adobe Stock's AI Studio. A concrete brand-consistency workflow for teams generating campaign variants from one hero image.

A live behind-the-scenes teardown of a fully automated AI content system, showing how the agent chain, tooling and handoffs are actually wired together. Useful reference for creatives building their own production automation.
Theo explains why he no longer works in a terminal, moving agent-driven building into a different surface entirely. A signal that the interface for agentic making is itself becoming a design problem.
